recordings.title: Poor Fellow Died in a Military Hospital
recordings.medium: 78 rpm shellac gramophone record / Ogg Vorbis
recordings.author: Lyrics: Grand Duke Konstantin Konstantinovich (K.R., 1885); traditional melody
recordings.description: Authentic 1909 gramophone recording of the soldier's lament poem by K.R. Nadezhda Plevitskaya performs with unadorned folk pathos the lonely death of an unnumbered recruit in an army infirmary, carried out in a deal coffin to an unrecorded common trench: 'Neither cross nor tombstone will tell where he fell asleep forever'. A central acoustic document for Plate Y (The Military Cenotaph).

recordings.title: Across the Wild Steppes of Transbaikalia
recordings.performer_ru: Историческая архивная запись (народный хор и солист)
recordings.author: I. K. Kondratyev (attrib., 1880s) / traditional Siberian exile song
recordings.description: Historic recording of the classic Siberian exile and convict song. Tells of a runaway convict who survived the road through endless marshes and steppes only to find his family house empty and his father long lying in the damp ground: 'Tears choked the poor fellow, / His father is long in the сырая земля.' Resonates directly with Plate P (Roads and Crossroads) and Plate M (The Empty House).

recordings.title: Song of the Volga Boatmen (Ei, Ukhnem)
recordings.medium: Victor 14901-A electrical 78 rpm shellac / Ogg Vorbis
recordings.author: Traditional Volga burlak chant, arr. M. Balakirev / F. Chaliapin
recordings.description: Feodor Chaliapin's legendary 1927 Victor electrical recording. The dragging, ponderous cadence of river burlaks leaning their chests into leather haulage straps, invoking the birch tree and Mother Volga in a ritualistic exertion bordering on death and chthonic weight. Connects to Plate O (Water, Marsh and River) and Plate D (The Table / Ritual labor).

recordings.title: Funeral Perebor (Church Bell Peal for the Departed)
recordings.performer: Northern Bell Ringing Tradition (Arkhangelsk / Kargopol canon)
recordings.medium: Physical modal synthesis / Ogg Vorbis & MP3
recordings.author: Traditional Russian Orthodox funeral toll (from treble zazvonny to bass blagovest)
recordings.description: The canonical Russian funeral bell toll (перебор): a slow, sequential progression from the highest treble bells (зазвонные) to the lowest bass bell (благовестник), symbolizing human life from childhood to old age, crowned by a unified choral strike of all bells signifying the sudden severance of life. Re-synthesized through modal bell acoustics with non-harmonic partials and natural doppler beatings. Central acoustic monument for Plate G (The Bell Tower) and Plate F (The Coffin).

recordings.title: Spiritual Verse: On the Parting of Soul from Body
recordings.title_ru: Духовный стих: О разлучении души с телом
recordings.performer: Old Believer Monodic Cantillating Tradition (Pomor / Vetka chant)
recordings.medium: Acoustic formant synthesis / Moorer-Schroeder chapel reverberation / Ogg Vorbis & MP3
recordings.author: Anonymous Old Believer penitential manuscript / Znameny monody
recordings.description: Reconstruction of the archaic spiritual verse sung beside the dying or during the reading of the Psalter over the deceased in Old Believer settlements of the Russian North: 'Увы мне, грешному человеку, како разлучается душа от тела...'. Monodic Dorian intonations with microtonal glides and pure acoustic fifth intervals resonant within a high timber chapel space. Central acoustic monument for Plate H (The Lament and Spiritual Verse) and Plate B (The Body).
